newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel approves plan to sell 25 pct stake in Bezeq.
newsitem.headline: Israel approves plan to sell 25 pct stake in Bezeq.

text.p: Israel on Thursday approved a plan to sell 25 percent of Bezeq, the country's main telecommunications carrier, reducing its holding to 51 percent by the end of the year, a government official said.
The news came as Bezeq Israel Telecom's board announced it had named Ami Erel managing director.
Erel, 50, an electronics engineer by training, was for the last seven years managing director of the Idan-Elitec group Idan provides telecommunications services and products.
Bezeq has seen its monopoly gradually whittled down over the years but retains monopolies in basic services and infrastructure.

Moshe Leon, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's chief economics adviser, said the plan to sell 25 percent of Bezeq called for selling part of the shares -- probably 10 percent -- through a public offering in the Israeli capital market.
The rest would be sold by means yet to be determined, he said.
Leon told Reuters that the domestic public flotation would be in two to three months. He refused to speculate on how the remaining shares would be sold.
The Israeli government holds 76 percent of Bezeq. The rest trades on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, although about half the float is controlled by Britain's Cable and Wireless PLC.
Israel has been in lengthy negotiations with Cable and Wireless over the British company's future role in Bezeq, but officials said no agreement had yet been reached.

"Erel thanked the directors and promised that he would do all in his power that also in the era of competition Bezeq would be Israel's biggest telecommunications company," the Bezeq statement on his appointment said.

He takes over from acting managing director Avi Hochman, who filled the post when a civil service watchdog committee refused to let Yoram Turbowicz take the job until he sat out a one-year cooling-off period because of a possible conflict of interest.
Turbowicz had been due to take over from Yitzhak Kaul on March 2. He subsequently said he would not accept the post.
Communications Minister Limor Livnat and other officials have been pushing hard to speed the privatisation of Bezeq.

Shares in the company were originally supposed to be floated in a global offering, but in February she approved a plan for a domestic offering on the grounds it could be done Government sources said they hoped they could raise about $500 million from the sale of the 25 percent stake. Bezeq's market capitalisation is $1.9 billion. Part of the proceeds might go to the company itself, they added.

Bezeq officials have said they would prefer a global offering, which would raise the company's profile in international financial markets. In addition, the weakness of the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange precludes floating all the shares domestically, officials have said.
